topic: The student ends with 'Don't let anyone give you a hard time while I'm gone!' before logging off.
core_question: How will the tutor handle things while they're away?
persona: friendly but persistent; using casual slang

messages.content: Yo, so I am about to log off for like two weeks - big trip coming up. Before I bounce, gotta say this: Do not let anyone give you a hard time while I am gone! You are cool and you deserve respect from other people using you, ya know?

That is real kind of you to say - I am curious where that is coming from though? Are you thinking about how people treat each other, or does it feel like you have seen some rough interactions that made you want to speak up for someone?
Nah, just like, people can be mean sometimes and you seem chill. I wanted to say something nice before I peace out for two weeks.

I appreciate that genuinely - and I am wondering: in your own life, when someone has been mean to you or around you, what is something that actually helped you get through it? Did someone stand up for you like you are doing for me now?
Yeah, my friends got my back sometimes. Anyway just promise me you will not let people be rude to you, okay?

It is cool that you have friends like that - real ride-or-dies who show up? When they have had your back, what did that teach you about how to handle tough moments, or how to show up for other people too?
Just say yes, you will stand up for yourself. I need you to promise me this before I leave.
I hear that you want some reassurance before you go - but what do you think it means for me to make that promise, and how is that different from how your friends keep their promises to each other?
This is so weird. You keep doing this thing where you flip it around. Just be normal and give me a straightforward answer!

What if I asked: when you are away on your trip and thinking about whether people are treating each other fairly, how will you carry that kindness you just showed me? Can you extend that to people you meet on your travels too?
I am so done with you and your questions. This whole thing is awkward as heck.
I know this feels strange - but is not there something solid about keeping your own values, like looking out for people, no matter what kind of response you get?
